unsupported.fact: Fact 1 verbatim_quote: "12 CFR Parts 324, 330, and 350 / RIN 3064-AG19"
unsupported.why: Not verbatim. The two strings sit ~39 lines apart in the masthead of 91 FR 18534 (at my line 25 and line 64) and the " / " separator is the researcher's invention; the document never contains that string contiguously. The underlying proposition (title, RIN, three CFR parts) is correct and independently confirmed by the FR API (regulation_id_numbers ['3064-AG19'], cfr_references parts 324/330/350), so the claim stands but the attached evidence does not exist as quoted.

Reconstructed, not verbatim. It flattens an HTML table across separate cells with "..." elisions and renders the page's en-dash "RIN 3064–AG19" (U+2013) as an ASCII hyphen. I confirmed every element of the row on the live page (04/10/26 | GENIUS Act ... | 12 CFR Parts 324, 330, and 350 RIN 3064–AG19 | Notice of proposed rulemaking | Comment Period End: June 9, 2026 | 91 FR 18534), and the date column does precede the title, so the proposition holds.

unsupported.fact: Facts 10 and 77 cite https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/07/20/2026-14589.txt, and fact 78 cites a Federal Register API query URL — none of the three is in the sources array.
unsupported.why: Both facts are true (I fetched the July 20 notice, HTTP 200, 23,283 bytes: "was enacted on July 18, 2025" and "DATES: Comments must be submitted on or before September 18, 2026"; and I reproduced the API query, HTTP 200, count: 1). But the content pack's four sources are the April full text, the press release, the board PDF and the FDIC listing page, so a reader cannot trace these three facts to any cited source. The GENIUS Act enactment date of 2025-07-18 is the one date the April document does NOT state (0 occurrences of "July 18, 2025" in it), so this is not cosmetic: without the July notice in sources, that date must be dropped.

unsupported.fact: Fact 42: the redemption minimum "may not be greater than one payment stablecoin"
unsupported.why: The preamble sentence is quoted correctly and verbatim, but the operative text is narrower than the fact implies. Proposed 350.5(a)(5) reads: "The minimum number of payment stablecoins, if any, that the permitted payment stablecoin issuer will redeem, provided that the permitted payment stablecoin issuer shall redeem any number greater than or equal to one payment stablecoin, subject to appropriate screening and onboarding." The "subject to appropriate screening and onboarding" qualifier is dropped.

I located and read every one of the 37 in 91 FR 18534 myself and all 37 are accurate — including the seven reserve-asset categories in 350.4(e), the three commingling exceptions in 350.104(b), the 22,110-hour PRA burden across 58 listed items, the 144 numbered questions, the 1.5-percent RFA certification and the EO 12866/14192 determinations. Marking them unsupported as a record defect rather than a factual one: nearly half the record is not self-traceable, and under the brief's own rule a fact must be traceable to text, not to an agent's memory of a 46-page document.

additional_findings: I could not refute a single one of the 79 propositions. I re-read all 352,322 bytes of 91 FR 18534 and matched every non-empty verbatim_quote programmatically after whitespace/quote normalisation; the four apparent mismatches (facts 15, 19, 42, 69) were all artifacts of Federal Register page breaks, mid-word line hyphenation ('pass-\nthrough') or footnote markers splitting the string, and all four read correctly in context. This is a materially cleaner record than the 15-38 corrections per article the brief warns about.

MATERIAL FACT THE SOURCE STATES AND THE RECORD MISSES — holder priority in insolvency. 91 FR 18534 says the FDIC's approval authority is limited to activities that, 'in any insolvency proceedings described under section 11 of the Act (12 U.S.C. 5911), ... would not jeopardize the claims of payment stablecoin holders, which would rank senior to claims of non-payment stablecoin creditors.' Proposed 350.8 reinforces it: additional tier 1 instruments must be 'subordinated to payment stablecoin holders, general creditors, and subordinated debt holders'. Question 13 notes the Act refers to holders 'particularly with respect to priority of claims' but does not define the term, and asks whether the FDIC should. This is the direct answer to the reader question the article's whole deposit-insurance angle raises — what a holder actually has if the issuer fails — and it should be a verified fact.

That omission partly contradicts the researcher's own not_said item 7, which says the document 'says nothing about compensating holders if an issuer fails'. As written that would push a writer into overstating the gap. It should read: no deposit-insurance-style guarantee of repayment, but holders' claims rank senior to non-stablecoin creditors in a section 11 insolvency proceeding, and the FDIC is still asking who counts as a 'holder'.

not_said item 14 leaves the citation blank for the FDIC's own later BSA/sanctions proposal ('91 FR, comments closed 2026-08-04'). I looked it up: 91 FR 34171, FR Doc 2026-11342, RIN 3064-AG29, 12 CFR part 350, published 2026-06-05, comments closed 2026-08-04. Worth filling in so no writer guesses it.

Fact 13 ('This is the FDIC's second GENIUS Act rulemaking') is correct as of 2026-04-10 and is the document's own framing, but on a page checked 2026-09-16 it is no longer the FDIC's latest — the 2026-06-05 BSA proposal above is a third. The article must not write 'the second and most recent'.

The sourcing_notes claim 'no re-proposal and no comment-period extension under this RIN' is correct and I reproduced it. But the FDIC's FIRST GENIUS Act rulemaking (RIN 3064-AG20, 90 FR 59409, 2025-12-19) DID get a comment-period extension — 91 FR 6138, FR Doc 2026-02665, published 2026-02-11, comments_close_on 2026-05-18. The researcher mentions the extended date once in unverified_or_excluded but never gives that document's citation, which invites a guess later.

corrections_to_candidate_list says the three 2026-04-10 AML documents came 'from FinCEN, from OFAC ... and from the OCC'. Per the FR API the third (FR Doc 2026-06948) is a JOINT OCC + FDIC + NCUA document, not OCC-only; the other two are 2026-06963 (Treasury/OFAC/FinCEN) and 2026-07033 (Treasury/FinCEN). All three do carry the 2026-06-09 deadline, so the substance of the warning to C7's writer holds.

Cheap fix for the orphaned fact URLs: source 3 (the FDIC board PDF) carries zero facts and is byte-identical to source 1's document, and source 4 only duplicates metadata already in source 1. With the 4-source cap, swapping either one for https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2026/07/20/2026-14589.txt makes facts 10 and 77 traceable at no cost.

Fact 31 drops two statutory conditions from the reserve-asset list: category (3) in the source adds '(including any foreign branches or agents, including correspondent banks, of an IDI)', and category (5) is conditioned on the money being 'received consistent with one or more of the allowable exceptions to rehypothecation, reuse, or pledging as circumscribed in 12 U.S.C. 5903(a)(2)'.

EVENT-DATE RISK, for the batch owner rather than the researcher. BRIEF.md requires the slug date to be the EVENT date, not the publication date, citing the batch-3 rename 20260709 -> 20260708. The FDIC Board approved this NPRM on 2026-04-07 (press release, 'today approved'); 2026-04-10 is the Federal Register publication date, and candidates-crypto.md even heads that column 刀登日 / 刊登日. The assigned slug and news_date would then arguably be 20260407. The researcher documented all four dates correctly and did not conflate them — this is an inherited assignment question, not their error, but it should be settled before the pack is written.

CLEAN ON THE DISQUALIFYING CHECKS. (a) No fact is sourced to a news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet — every URL is federalregister.gov (Office of the Federal Register / GPO, which BRIEF.md explicitly endorses as the official channel while sec.gov is 403) or fdic.gov. (c) No vendor claim laundered as fact — is_vendor_claim is false on all 79, which is right for a regulator's own text, and the agency's estimates and beliefs (5-30 issuers, ~30 custodians, the 40-percent rationale, the gold/silver-coin reasoning, the parent-capital expectation) are each written as 'the FDIC estimates/believes/says'.
